section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Arizona, which agency administers driver's licenses?
options: a:The Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV),b:The Motor Vehicle Division (MVD),c:The Department of Transportation (ADOT),d:The Department of Public Safety (DPS)
note: Arizona driver's licenses are administered by the Motor Vehicle Division (MVD), not a 'DMV.' This state-specific distinction is commonly tested because most states use the DMV name.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum age to apply for a learner's permit in Arizona?
options: a:14,b:15,c:15 and a half,d:16
note: Arizona requires applicants to be at least 15½ years old before applying for a learner's permit. This is an important GDL milestone — applicants must have held the permit for at least 6 months before applying for a provisional license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on most urban streets in Arizona when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:20 mph,b:25 mph,c:30 mph,d:35 mph
note: Arizona sets the default speed limit in urban and residential areas at 25 mph when no other limit is posted. Always check posted signs — many streets have limits posted that differ from the default.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on an Arizona highway during a haboob (massive dust storm). What should you do?
options: a:Pull over, turn off all lights, and stay in your vehicle,b:Pull completely off the road, turn off all lights, take your foot off the brake, and stay in the vehicle,c:Turn on your hazard lights and continue driving slowly,d:Speed up to get through the storm as quickly as possible
note: Arizona's 'Pull Aside, Stay Alive' rule for haboobs requires drivers to pull completely off the road, turn off ALL lights (including hazard flashers and brake lights), take your foot off the brake, and wait out the storm. Leaving lights on causes other drivers to follow you — believing you are on the road — leading to fatal chain-reaction crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for drivers age 21 and older in Arizona?
note: Arizona sets the per se DUI limit at 0.08% BAC for adult drivers. Arizona also has an 'Extreme DUI' designation for a BAC of 0.15% or higher, which carries significantly enhanced penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Arizona, what must you do when you encounter a dust devil (small, spinning dust column) on the road?
options: a:Accelerate through it quickly,b:Slow down and move away from it if possible — it can briefly reduce visibility,c:Stop and wait for it to pass,d:It poses no hazard — maintain speed
note: Dust devils can briefly reduce visibility and sometimes contain debris. Arizona drivers are advised to slow down and steer away when possible. While smaller than haboobs, they can still cause a sudden loss of visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arizona's GDL program, what nighttime driving restriction applies to drivers under 18 with a provisional license?
options: a:No nighttime restriction applies,b:No driving between 10 PM and 5 AM for the first 6 months of the provisional license,c:No driving between midnight and 5 AM for the first 6 months,d:No nighttime driving at all during the provisional phase
note: For the first 6 months after receiving an Arizona provisional license, drivers under 18 may not drive between 10 PM and 5 AM unless accompanied by a licensed driver age 21 or older, or driving to/from work or a school activity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit on most Arizona interstates in rural areas?
options: a:65 mph,b:70 mph,c:75 mph,d:80 mph
note: Most rural Arizona interstates have a posted speed limit of 75 mph for passenger vehicles. Some segments allow 85 mph where posted. Always check posted signs — limits vary by location and vehicle type.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are approaching a roundabout in Arizona. What is the correct procedure?
options: a:Vehicles already in the roundabout must yield to entering vehicles,b:Yield to vehicles already circulating in the roundabout, then enter when safe,c:Traffic in the roundabout alternates turns with entering traffic,d:Stop at the entry and wait for the roundabout to be fully clear
note: In a roundabout, traffic already circulating inside has the right of way. Entering vehicles must yield, check for gaps, and merge when safe. You do not need to wait for the entire circle to be clear — just for a safe gap in the flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane Arizona road, you see a solid yellow line on your side of the center. What does this mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted when the road ahead is clear,b:Passing is prohibited — do not cross the line to pass,c:Passing is permitted only at speeds above 45 mph,d:The road becomes one-way ahead
note: A solid yellow line on your side prohibits crossing the center line to pass another vehicle. Only a dashed yellow line on your side signals that passing is permitted when safe. This rule applies throughout the United States.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do if your vehicle's tires hit a soft shoulder on an Arizona highway?
options: a:Brake hard to regain control,b:Jerk the steering wheel back onto the pavement immediately,c:Ease off the gas, grip the wheel firmly, and gradually steer back onto the pavement at low speed,d:Accelerate to pop back onto the road
note: If your tires drop off the pavement onto a soft shoulder, ease off the gas and hold the wheel steady. Jerking back onto the pavement at highway speed can cause a rollover. Instead, gradually reduce speed and steer gently back onto the road once it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum following distance recommended for normal driving conditions in Arizona?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Arizona recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. In heavy rain, blowing dust, or other reduced-visibility conditions common in Arizona, increase following distance significantly — poor visibility sharply reduces reaction time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arizona law, a driver under 21 found driving with a BAC of 0.00%–0.08% will:
options: a:Face no charges if below 0.08%,b:Face DUI charges under the 'any spirituous liquor' law since any alcohol is illegal for those under 21,c:Receive a warning only on the first offense,d:Face a minor infraction fine but no license action
note: Arizona law prohibits drivers under 21 from having any spirituous liquor in their system while driving — meaning any detectable alcohol is illegal for underage drivers regardless of the 0.08% adult standard. This is a state-specific zero tolerance rule.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on an Arizona road and see a cattle crossing sign. What should you expect?
options: a:Cattle have the right of way on the road — you must stop for them,b:Cattle may be present on or near the road — slow down and prepare to stop,c:The sign only applies at night when cattle are hard to see,d:Accelerate through the area quickly before cattle reach the road
note: Cattle crossing signs warn that livestock may be present on or near the road, particularly on rural Arizona highways near ranches. Slow down, prepare to stop, and never try to drive around cattle on the roadway — they are unpredictable and can cause severe crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Arizona, when must you turn on your headlights?
options: a:Only after dark,b:From sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is less than 500 feet,c:Only in rain or fog,d:Only when driving on interstate highways at night
note: Arizona requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and any time visibility is reduced to less than 500 feet — such as in rain, dust, or fog. Turning headlights on early (before sunset) and keeping them on after sunrise in poor conditions is always the safer choice.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can you turn right on a red light in Arizona?
options: a:No, right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:Yes, after a complete stop and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Yes, without stopping if no vehicles are in the intersection,d:Only between 7 AM and 9 PM
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Arizona after a complete stop, yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic. Some intersections have 'No Turn on Red' signs — always check before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches from behind?
options: a:Speed up to the next intersection and turn off the road,b:Stop immediately in your current lane,c:Pull to the right edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed,d:Move to the left lane and reduce speed by 10 mph
note: Arizona law requires drivers to immediately pull to the right side of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches. Remain stopped until the vehicle has fully passed before resuming travel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does Arizona's Move Over law require when passing a stopped emergency vehicle on a multi-lane highway?
options: a:Slow to 15 mph and maintain your lane,b:Move one lane away from the stopped vehicle if safe; if not, slow to a safe speed,c:Stop completely and wait for the vehicle to leave,d:Move over only for police vehicles, not tow trucks
note: Arizona's Move Over law requires drivers to vacate the lane adjacent to a stopped emergency, law enforcement, or highway maintenance vehicle with flashing lights. If a lane change is not safely possible, slow down to a speed that is safe for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What shape and color identifies a warning sign in Arizona?
options: a:Red octagon,b:White rectangle,c:Yellow diamond,d:Orange rectangle
note: Warning signs are yellow diamond-shaped signs that alert drivers to potential hazards ahead such as sharp curves, school zones, and pedestrian crossings. The yellow diamond shape is a universal standard used throughout the United States.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are making a left turn at an intersection. When do you have the right of way?
options: a:Always — the turning vehicle always has the right of way,b:When oncoming traffic has stopped or there is a clear gap with no oncoming traffic,c:When you have been waiting longer than 30 seconds,d:Only when a left-turn arrow is displayed
note: Left-turning vehicles must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians in the crosswalk. You may proceed only when oncoming traffic has cleared or stopped, or when a protected left-turn arrow is displayed. Left turns without a protected signal require patience and caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Arizona, what is the default speed limit on open highway roads not posted as interstates?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: Arizona's default speed limit on undivided rural highways not posted otherwise is 65 mph for passenger vehicles. Always check posted signs — some stretches may be posted at lower limits due to curves, grades, or construction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking on a street, your wheels must be within how many inches of the curb in Arizona?
options: a:6 inches,b:12 inches,c:18 inches,d:24 inches
note: Arizona law requires parallel-parked vehicles to be within 18 inches of the right-hand curb or edge of the road. Parking too far from the curb obstructs traffic and is an infraction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as three other vehicles — one on your right, one across from you, and one on your left. Who goes first?
options: a:The vehicle going straight has priority,b:The vehicle on your right goes first,c:The vehicle on your left goes last,d:All vehicles on your right and left yield to you since you arrived simultaneously
note: When multiple vehicles arrive simultaneously at a 4-way stop, the right-of-way goes to the vehicle on the right. If all four arrive at once, the same yield-to-the-right rule applies progressively until all vehicles have moved through safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arizona's implied consent law, refusing to take a chemical test after a DUI stop will result in:
options: a:No penalty — refusal is a legal right,b:A 1-year license suspension for first refusal,c:Only a fine, with no license action,d:A warning on your driving record
note: Arizona's implied consent law means that driving on public roads constitutes consent to chemical testing. A first-offense refusal results in a 1-year license suspension, separate from any DUI charges. Refusal can also be presented as evidence of guilt in court.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when approaching a school bus stopped with flashing red lights on a two-lane Arizona road?
options: a:Stop only if driving behind the bus,b:Slow to 15 mph and proceed carefully,c:Stop in both directions at least 20 feet from the bus and wait until lights stop flashing,d:Stop only if children are visibly crossing the road
note: Arizona law requires vehicles in both directions on an undivided road to stop at least 20 feet from a school bus displaying flashing red lights. You may not proceed until the lights stop and the stop arm retracts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to pass a vehicle on a two-lane Arizona highway. Which of the following is a legal reason to pass on the right?
options: a:The left lane is occupied by a slower vehicle,b:The vehicle ahead is turning left and the right side of the road is clear and wide enough,c:There is no legal situation — passing on the right is always prohibited,d:When the vehicle ahead is driving more than 10 mph below the speed limit
note: In Arizona, passing on the right is permitted only when the vehicle ahead is turning left and there is sufficient room on the right side of the road. You may not use the shoulder to pass on the right — only paved roadway space counts.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid white line in the middle of the road separates two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may:
options: a:Cross it freely to change lanes,b:Cross it only in an emergency or when merging near an intersection,c:Never cross it under any circumstances,d:Cross it only if you signal first
note: A solid white line indicates that lane changes are discouraged in that area — typically near intersections, on-ramps, or other areas where weaving is dangerous. You should avoid crossing a solid white line except in an emergency.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arizona law, what is the penalty for a first-offense 'Extreme DUI' (BAC 0.15% or higher)?
options: a:Same as a standard DUI — no distinction is made at the state level,b:Enhanced mandatory minimum jail time, higher fines, and mandatory ignition interlock device,c:License suspension only — no jail time for the first offense,d:Community service only
note: Arizona's Extreme DUI law carries mandatory minimum jail time of 30 days, higher fines, and a required ignition interlock device — more severe than a standard first DUI. Arizona is known for having some of the toughest DUI penalties in the nation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in Arizona and need to change lanes on a highway. What is the correct sequence?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, check blind spot, move smoothly into the new lane,b:Signal, accelerate, then move into the new lane,c:Check mirrors and immediately move into the new lane if clear,d:Move into the new lane, then signal so drivers know your intention
note: The correct lane-change sequence is: check mirrors, activate your turn signal, check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder, and then move smoothly into the new lane when it is clear. Signaling first warns other drivers of your intent before you move.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Arizona, how long before a turn must you signal?
options: a:50 feet,b:100 feet,c:200 feet,d:300 feet
note: Arizona requires drivers to signal at least 100 feet before turning. On higher-speed roads or when traffic is heavy, signaling earlier gives other drivers more time to adjust. Failing to signal is a traffic violation and a common cause of crashes.

question: In very foggy conditions you should slow down and use which lights?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Low beam headlights are correct in fog because their light pattern aims down toward the road and reduces glare. High beams shine more light straight ahead and up, which reflects off the fog droplets and back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Hazard/emergency flashers are not a substitute for proper headlight use while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signals when parking next to a curb?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.,d:Never required when parking.
note: You should signal any time you change your position in traffic, including when pulling toward a curb to park and when pulling away from the curb to re-enter traffic. Signaling both movements lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians anticipate your path and adjust safely.

question: How must you treat an approaching flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield as needed, and proceed when safe.,b:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.,c:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and then proceed only when it is safe. You do not remain stopped indefinitely; you may go after stopping and yielding as required.

question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light, what must you do?
options: a:Wait for the green light before proceeding.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. You are not required to stop, but you must slow down, be prepared to yield, and carefully check for cross traffic and pedestrians before entering the intersection.

question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, you should:
options: a:Set the parking brake.,b:Press down hard on the accelerator.,c:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.
note: Before stopping, you should check your mirrors so you know where vehicles behind and beside you are. This helps you brake smoothly and early, reducing the risk of being rear-ended and allowing you to adjust if someone is following too closely.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot you should:
options: a:Stay in the driver's blind spot.,b:Keep a steady pace.,c:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
note: Staying in another driver’s blind spot is dangerous because they cannot see you and may change lanes into your vehicle. You should either move ahead or drop back so that you are clearly visible in their mirrors.

question: After having several beers, only what will reduce alcohol's effects?
options: a:Drinking several cups of coffee.,b:Waiting several hours.,c:Taking a cold shower.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol. Coffee, cold showers, or other tricks do not lower your blood alcohol concentration or restore safe driving ability.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
options: a:25 feet,b:30 feet,c:15 feet
note: You must keep a clear space around fire hydrants so firefighters can connect hoses quickly in an emergency. In many states, you may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To safely enter a gap in highway traffic you should:
options: a:Assume gaps will appear automatically.,b:Speed up and force drivers to make room.,c:Watch only vehicles behind the intended gap.,d:Check traffic behind and to the sides, then be sure there is enough space ahead to merge safely.
note: To enter a gap in highway traffic safely, you must know what is happening all around your vehicle. Check behind you and to the sides, then judge the space in front to be sure there is enough room to accelerate smoothly into the gap without forcing other drivers to brake suddenly.

question: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors and also:
options: a:Never look over your right shoulder.,b:Always slow down in your traffic lane.,c:Glance over your shoulder.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; there are blind spots along the sides. Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure the lane is clear.

question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from both directions.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:The dashed side must yield to the solid side.,d:Passing is permitted only from the side next to the dashed line.
note: A dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the dashed line. Drivers on the side with the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not start across an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red:
options: a:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.,b:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.,c:Under any circumstances.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it without stopping. Even with a green light, you may not pull into the intersection if doing so would leave your vehicle blocking cross traffic when the light changes.

question: What is the only thing that will lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drinking caffeine,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Time
note: Only time lowers your BAC because your body needs time to metabolize alcohol. Coffee, food, cold showers, or exercise may make you feel more awake but do not speed up the elimination of alcohol from your system.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:Because it is illegal to turn off your signal before finishing the turn.,b:So other road users know your intentions.,c:Because it is unsafe to turn off a signal early.,d:To avoid using your mirrors.
note: You should signal continuously before and during a turn so that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians clearly understand your intentions. This advance warning helps them adjust speed or position to avoid conflicts.

question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:
options: a:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.,b:Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.,c:Avoid the puddle if possible.
note: If you see a deep puddle ahead, steer around it if you can do so safely. Deep water can cause hydroplaning, loss of control, or mechanical damage. If you must drive through, slow down and proceed carefully.

question: As your driving speed increases, what becomes more important?
options: a:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Change lanes frequently.
note: At higher speeds you cover more distance in less time, so hazards appear and reach you more quickly. Looking well ahead gives you extra time to see problems early and brake or change lanes smoothly instead of making sudden, unsafe maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Prior to entering a curve you should:
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Activate your turn signal.
note: You should slow down before you enter a curve so your tires can grip the road and you can steer smoothly. Braking hard while turning can cause skids or loss of control, especially on wet or loose surfaces.

question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:
options: a:Only if other traffic is minimal.,b:Only when children are present.,c:Only during school hours.,d:At all times.
note: School crossing guards have legal authority to direct traffic where they are assigned. Whenever they are on duty and giving directions, you must obey their signals, regardless of traffic volume, time of day, or whether you see children in the crosswalk.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of their way.,b:Challenge them.,c:Speed up.
note: When you encounter an aggressive driver, focus on safety, not winning or teaching them a lesson. Safely move out of their way, avoid eye contact or gestures, and do not speed up or challenge them, which can escalate the situation and increase crash risk.

question: What is a crosswalk?
options: a:An area designated for road construction workers.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.
note: A crosswalk is the part of the road set aside for pedestrians to cross. It may be marked with painted lines or be an unmarked extension of the sidewalk across an intersection, where pedestrians still have the right to cross.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) rises, you become:
options: a:More intoxicated.,b:More coordinated.,c:More sober.
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) is the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream. As BAC increases, your judgment, reaction time, coordination, and self-control all get worse. You become more impaired and more intoxicated, not more coordinated or sober.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait until they are raised.,b:Slow down and drive around the gates.,c:Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.
note: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you must stop and stay stopped behind the gate line. Never drive around or under lowered gates, even if you do not see a train. Proceed only after the lights stop flashing and the gates are fully raised, and you have checked that the tracks are clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Often,b:Never; it confuses other drivers.,c:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.
note: Right-of-way is something you are given, not something you take. Even if you are legally entitled to go first, you should yield whenever it helps prevent a collision. Never insist on your right-of-way if another driver is not yielding; avoiding a crash is always more important than being technically correct.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the lane on your right.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane highways, the right lane is generally for slower traffic and the left lane for passing. If you are in the center lane and vehicles are passing you on both sides, you are likely going slower than the flow of traffic. When safe, move to the right lane so faster traffic can pass on the left.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,b:All of the above.,c:Tranquilizers
note: Many substances can impair driving, not just illegal drugs. Tranquilizers can slow your reactions and make you drowsy. Cough syrups and cold medicines with codeine or antihistamines can also cause drowsiness, blurred vision, and slower reaction time. Always read medication labels and avoid driving if a drug can make you sleepy or affect alertness.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,b:Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.
note: Even without a marked crosswalk, drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing their lane and allow them to cross safely.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility ahead, you should slow down and turn on which lights?
options: a:Headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: When dust or smoke reduces visibility, you should slow down and turn on your low‑beam headlights so you can see and be seen. Parking lights alone are too dim, and emergency flashers do not replace headlights for lighting the road or making your vehicle clearly visible from all angles.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what is the safest choice?
options: a:Open a window.,b:Drink something with caffeine.,c:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.
note: To avoid fatigued driving, take breaks or switch drivers; short measures like caffeine or windows are not reliable substitutes for rest.

question: If the rear of your car begins skidding to the left while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Steer to the left.,b:Steer to the right.,c:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.
note: If the rear of your car skids to one side, you should steer in the same direction the rear is sliding. This helps realign the vehicle with your intended path. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering, which can make the skid worse.

question: Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
options: a:45 miles per hour.,b:40 miles per hour.,c:35 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can start at about 35 mph when there is enough water on the road for your tires to ride on top of it instead of gripping the surface. Reducing speed in wet conditions helps your tires maintain contact with the road and improves control.

question: A steady red arrow displayed on a traffic light means:
options: a:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.,b:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.,c:Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to go in the direction of the arrow. You must wait until the arrow turns green (or is replaced by a signal that allows movement) before making the turn.

question: To turn quickly and safely, how should your hands be positioned on the steering wheel?
options: a:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.,b:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.,c:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
note: For normal and quick turns, your hands should be on opposite sides of the steering wheel (commonly around the 9 and 3 o’clock positions). This gives you the best control, balance, and ability to steer smoothly and quickly if needed.

question: When driving on snowy or icy roads you should:
options: a:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than usual.,b:Drive as on dry roads.,c:Use cruise control.,d:Brake abruptly to stop quickly.
note: On snow or ice, you should slow down and make all speed and steering changes gradually to avoid skidding. Do not use cruise control on slippery roads because it can cause you to lose control. Brake gently and early; if you do not have ABS, use light, repeated braking instead of a hard, sudden stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.,b:Use your side mirror.,c:Use the inside rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, called blind spots. Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, you must:
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in lane.,b:Move into the right lane and slow down.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.,d:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or a siren, you must pull over to the right side of the road and stop, clear of any intersection, and remain stopped until the vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

question: If you are feeling fatigued while driving, you should:
options: a:Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.,b:Increase the volume of your radio.,c:Increase your speed to reach your destination more quickly.
note: If you start to feel drowsy or fatigued while driving, the safe choice is to get off the road and rest. Pull into a safe parking area, stop driving, and take a short nap or switch drivers. Turning up the radio or trying to push through fatigue does not restore alertness and greatly increases your crash risk.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means which vehicles may pass?
options: a:Vehicles in both directions may pass.,b:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.,c:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line, and prohibited for traffic on the side with the solid line. Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and you may only cross them to pass when the line next to your lane is broken and it is safe.

question: If you encounter a severe dust storm, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.,b:Turn on your high beams.,c:Slow down and pull completely off the road
note: In a severe dust storm where visibility is greatly reduced, you should slow down and pull completely off the roadway, as far to the right as possible, and stop. Turn off your lights and take your foot off the brake so other drivers are not drawn toward you, stay buckled, and wait until visibility improves before re-entering traffic.

question: If your vehicle's wheels run off the pavement, what is the first action to take?
options: a:Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge back onto the pavement.,b:Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. Ease off the accelerator and brake gently. Once you have slowed and the car is under control, carefully steer back onto the pavement when there is a clear gap in traffic. Jerking the wheel or braking hard can cause you to lose control or skid.

question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent:
options: a:Won't have any effect on your driving.,b:Won't put other drivers at risk.,c:Will double your chances of having an accident.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol in your system can affect judgment, reaction time, and coordination. A blood alcohol concentration around 0.02% has been shown in safety research to measurably increase crash risk compared with a 0.00% BAC, especially for inexperienced drivers. Because any alcohol can impair driving ability, the safest choice is not to drive after drinking at all.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should your following distance compare to following a passenger car?
options: a:Farther behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.,b:Closer behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.,c:To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.
note: Large trucks have bigger blind spots and need more distance to stop. When you follow a truck, leave more space than you would behind a passenger car so you can see the road ahead and have enough time to react.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, you should:
options: a:Reduce speed,b:Turn on high beams and continue.,c:Speed up to pass through quickly.,d:Turn on four-way flashers and continue driving.
note: If smoke or dust is blocking your view of the road, you must slow down immediately. Be prepared to pull completely off the roadway, turn on your hazard lights, and stop if you cannot see well enough to drive safely. Never speed up or continue at normal speed when visibility is severely reduced.

question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing, when may vehicles that are stopped behind it proceed?
options: a:When all students are off the bus.,b:When the stop arm is retracted and the bus starts moving.,c:When the bus driver waves you on.,d:When the stop arm is retracted.
note: When a school bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must remain stopped. You may proceed only after the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is fully retracted, and then only when it is clearly safe to move.

question: How do you check your blind spots?
options: a:By looking in your side mirrors.,b:By turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:By looking only in your rearview mirror.,d:By using your high beams.
note: Mirrors do not show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle. To check your blind spots before changing lanes or merging, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, you may safely return to your lane when you:
options: a:Can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.,c:Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the passed vehicle (or its headlights at night) in your rearview mirror and you have enough space to return without cutting the other driver off.

question: Why should you increase following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,b:Because other drivers will pull behind large vehicles.,c:To get caught in the vehicle's slipstream.,d:Because large vehicles always stop suddenly.
note: Large trucks and buses block your view of the road ahead. By leaving extra space, you can see around them better and have more time to react if traffic slows or stops. The extra distance also helps ensure the truck driver can see you in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:
options: a:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,b:Improve traffic flow.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can be just as dangerous as speeding. It forces other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly, increasing the risk of crashes. If you must drive slower, use the right lane and match the general flow when it is safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a main roadway from a private road, drivers should:
options: a:Enter at high speed to merge quickly.,b:Yield to traffic already on the road.,c:Assume they have the right-of-way.,d:Honk to make other drivers move.
note: When entering a main road from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop if necessary and yield to all traffic already on the roadway and to pedestrians on sidewalks. Vehicles already on the main road have the right-of-way; you may only enter when it is safe.

question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving in work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle only.,b:Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment only.,c:Both tailgating another vehicle and failing to watch for workers and moving equipment.
note: Work zones often have narrowed lanes, changing traffic patterns, and workers close to moving vehicles. Following too closely reduces your time to react, and not watching carefully for workers and equipment can lead to serious crashes. Always slow down, increase following distance, and stay alert.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Turn off the ignition.,b:Ease up on the gas pedal.,c:Brake as hard as possible.
note: In a skid, sudden braking or steering can make you lose even more control. Gently easing off the accelerator helps the tires regain traction. Steer smoothly in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go and avoid slamming on the brakes unless your vehicle has ABS and you are trained to use firm, steady pressure.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing, you should:
options: a:Beep your horn.,b:See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:Flash your headlights.,d:Signal and immediately move over.
note: After you pass another vehicle, do not move back into your original lane until you can clearly see both of the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror and you have checked that it is safe. This ensures you have enough space and do not cut the other driver off.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on at night and you are affected, you should:
options: a:Look straight ahead into the headlights.,b:Flash your high beams in response.,c:Look toward the right edge of your lane.,d:Look toward the left edge of your lane.
note: When an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, avoid looking directly at the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use it as a guide while still watching traffic with your peripheral vision. This reduces temporary blindness from the bright lights and helps you stay in your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.,b:When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,c:When the yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.
note: You may cross the centerline to pass only when the broken yellow line is on your side of the road and you have enough clear distance to pass safely. A solid yellow line on your side means passing is prohibited, even if the other side has a broken line.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Traffic control devices.,b:Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.,c:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly turn your head to check these areas so you do not move into a space already occupied by another vehicle.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is worn, what problem may occur?
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering only.,d:Engine overheating.
note: A worn or damaged suspension system can cause poor vehicle control, excessive bouncing, and reduced stability, especially when turning or stopping. This makes the vehicle harder to handle and increases the risk of losing control in emergency situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait until there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic and the crosswalk is clear, or until a signal specifically gives you a protected left turn.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline you may:
options: a:You must stay within your lane.,b:Change lanes only from the left lane.,c:Cross the centerline to change lanes.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling.

question: Before driving, remove snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:Just the windshield and passenger window.,b:Just the windshield.,c:All windows.
note: Before driving in snow or icy conditions, clear all windows and mirrors so you have a full, unobstructed view in every direction. This helps you see other road users and prevents snow or ice from sliding and blocking your view while driving.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, how should you use it?
options: a:Use only the lap belt.,b:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: In a two-part safety belt system, always wear both the lap and shoulder belts. The lap belt should be low and snug across the hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the chest and shoulder. Using both parts together provides the best protection in a crash.

question: Which practice best describes where a driver should look while driving?
options: a:Stare directly in front of the car.,b:Only focus on the middle of the road.,c:Continuously scan ahead, to the sides, and behind.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan the entire traffic scene: far ahead, to both sides, and behind. This helps you spot hazards early, adjust speed and position smoothly, and avoid last‑second maneuvers.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?
options: a:Because it takes a quarter mile to stop.,b:To see potential hazards earlier.,c:To help you keep up with traffic speed.,d:To avoid checking mirrors frequently.
note: On freeways you are traveling at higher speeds, so hazards develop more quickly and it takes longer to react and slow or stop. Looking farther ahead gives you more time to see brake lights, congestion, or debris and adjust your speed or lane position smoothly instead of making sudden maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Turning right on a red light is permitted:
options: a:Only on a divided road.,b:Except where prohibited by a sign.,c:Only where indicated by a sign.
note: In most U.S. states, you may turn right on a red light after coming to a complete stop and yielding to pedestrians and cross traffic, unless a sign says “No Turn on Red” or otherwise prohibits it. Always check for signs and make sure the way is clear before turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, how do you know you have enough space to return to the lane?
options: a:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.,b:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,c:If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, you should not move back into the lane until you have enough space ahead of the vehicle you passed. A common rule is to wait until you can see both of the passed vehicle’s headlights in your inside rearview mirror. This indicates you have created a safe following distance before returning to the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should never change lanes while:
options: a:Within an intersection.,b:While your vehicle is moving.,c:On a multilane roadway.
note: You should not change lanes while you are in the middle of an intersection because traffic is merging and crossing from several directions, and drivers expect you to maintain your lane through the intersection. If you need to change lanes, do it before you enter or after you exit the intersection, when movements are more predictable and you can check mirrors and blind spots safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers must obey instructions from:
options: a:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,b:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
note: Flaggers at construction or work zones are authorized to control traffic and their instructions have the same legal force as traffic signals or signs. You must follow their hand signals or signs, even if they differ from normal traffic lights or lane markings, to move safely through the work area.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Brace yourself.,b:Press your head against the head restraint.,c:Release your seat belt.
note: You should never release your seat belt when a collision is about to occur. The belt keeps you from being thrown forward and greatly reduces injury. In a likely rear-end collision, keep your seat belt fastened, brace yourself, and press your head firmly against the head restraint to reduce whiplash.

question: A stopped school bus ahead on your side of the road is flashing red lights. What must you do?
options: a:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,b:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road is stopped with red lights flashing, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Passing a stopped school bus with red lights flashing is illegal and extremely dangerous because children may be crossing the road.

question: Which behavior may indicate an aggressive driver?
options: a:Their tendency to drive slowly.,b:Their erratic and improper lane changes.,c:The number of passengers in their car.
note: Aggressive drivers often show their behavior through unsafe driving actions, such as frequent, sudden, or improper lane changes, tailgating, speeding, and failing to yield. The number of passengers or simply driving slowly does not by itself indicate aggressive driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless a sign prohibits it, from where may you turn left on a red light?
options: a:From a one-way road to a one-way road.,b:From a two-way road to a one-way road.,c:Except in school zones.
note: In many states, you may turn left on a red light only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after coming to a complete stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians. This is only allowed where it is not prohibited by signs or local law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:Never required if no train is visible.,b:Only in cities with frequent train traffic.,c:When there isn't room on the other side to completely clear the tracks.,d:If you are transporting two or more young children.
note: You must never stop on railroad tracks. If there is not enough room on the far side of the tracks for your vehicle to completely clear them, you must stop and wait before the tracks until you can cross safely in one continuous movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are approaching an intersection at the posted speed limit and the light turns yellow you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to cross before it turns red.,c:Slow down and proceed through without caution.
note: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution and do not speed up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Driving much more slowly than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:A good idea if the weather is bad.,b:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,c:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake or make sudden lane changes and risky passing maneuvers. If you must drive more slowly, keep right and use turnouts where available so faster traffic can pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Slow and yield the right-of-way.,b:Treat it as a green light.,c:Drive carefully through the intersection.,d:Come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, then yield to any traffic or pedestrians in or close to the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When the driver you passed waves you back.,b:When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your inside rearview mirror.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,d:After you have signaled for three seconds.
note: After passing, do not move back into your lane until you are sure you have enough space ahead of the vehicle you passed. A good rule is to wait until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle, including both headlights, in your rearview mirror before returning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle in the same direction, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When the passed driver signals you to move back.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,d:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, you should not return to the right lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and you have checked that it is safe. This ensures you are not cutting too closely in front of the other driver.

question: To prevent hydroplaning on wet roads, what is the best action?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Move to the shoulder when it starts to rain.,c:Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride up on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. The faster you drive on wet pavement, the more likely this is to occur. Slowing down in the rain and on standing water helps your tires cut through the water and maintain traction, greatly reducing the risk of hydroplaning.

question: Which of the following will reduce a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
options: a:Drinking caffeine,b:Time,c:Eating foods high in fat
note: Only time lowers a person’s blood alcohol content. Once alcohol is in the bloodstream, the body must metabolize it, and this happens at a fairly steady rate. Coffee, food, cold showers, or any other tricks do not speed up this process. A person may feel more awake after caffeine or food, but they are still impaired until enough time has passed for the alcohol to be eliminated.

question: You plan a right turn and a pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross. What must you do?
options: a:Wait until the person crosses the street.,b:Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.,c:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes are visually impaired and have the right-of-way. When you plan to turn and such a pedestrian is waiting to cross, you must remain stopped and allow them to fully cross the street before you turn. Do not honk, call out directions, or try to guide them; simply wait until they are safely out of your path.

question: When backing up you should:
options: a:Press hard on the gas pedal.,b:Look through the rear window.,c:Rely only on your rearview mirror.
note: When backing up, you should move slowly and look directly where you are going. Place your right arm over the back of the passenger seat and turn your body so you can look straight out the rear window. Mirrors alone do not show the full area behind your vehicle, and pressing hard on the gas can cause you to lose control or hit something you cannot see.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving distracting?
options: a:It makes the driver worry about call cost.,b:It helps drivers stay alert.,c:It draws the attention of other drivers.,d:It occupies the driver's eyes and attention.
note: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it takes your attention away from the road. Talking, texting, or handling the phone can distract your mind from driving, your eyes from watching traffic, and your hands from steering. This combination of mental, visual, and manual distraction greatly increases the chance of a crash.

question: To improve visibility reduced by rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Low beam headlights are best in rain or fog because they aim light down toward the road and create less glare. High beams reflect off water droplets or fog and can make it harder to see, and parking lights alone are not sufficient for visibility or safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate, after checking for a gap, signaling, and adjusting speed, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for the lane to clear before merging.,b:Merge carefully into the gap.,c:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed since you have the right-of-way.
note: When entering an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, check your mirrors and blind spot, and then merge carefully into a safe gap. Do not stop in the acceleration lane unless absolutely necessary, and do not assume other drivers must yield to you.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, a motorist should:
options: a:Continue; vehicles have right-of-way.,b:Wait until the pedestrians have crossed the street.,c:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.,d:Honk to get them to move faster.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. Slow down or stop as needed and wait until the pedestrians have completely crossed your lane and the crosswalk is clear before proceeding. Never drive around pedestrians in the crosswalk or try to force them to hurry.

question: On a solid green arrow you must:
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection.,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,c:Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
note: A solid green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian already in the intersection. Do not enter the intersection until it is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
options: a:No one.,b:Overtaking cars.,c:Oncoming cars.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, unless you have a specific signal giving you a protected left turn. Wait for a safe gap before turning so you do not cut off approaching vehicles.

question: To whom should you give the right-of-way regarding pedestrians?
options: a:Any pedestrian in a marked or unmarked crosswalk at an intersection.,b:Only pedestrians in a marked crosswalk.,c:Pedestrians only if they have a crossing guard present.
note: You must always yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks, and you must use extra care for any pedestrian in the roadway. However, you are not required to yield to a pedestrian who suddenly steps into traffic where there is no crosswalk and no reasonable time to stop. The safest rule is to be prepared to stop for any pedestrian, but the legal right‑of‑way is focused on crosswalks and intersections.

question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:When visibility ahead is limited.,b:If you might hit another vehicle.,c:Near blind pedestrians.,d:When another driver is merging.
note: You should use your horn to warn others when there is a risk of a collision, such as when visibility is limited or you might hit another vehicle. You should not use your horn around blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog, because the sudden sound can be confusing and they rely heavily on sound cues from traffic. Instead, slow down, yield, and pass only when it is clearly safe.

question: What are truck \no zones\"?"
options: a:Areas where there are several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.,b:Areas with sufficient space to travel behind the truck.,c:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or restrict a truck's ability to stop and maneuver safely.
note: Truck “No Zones” are the large blind spots around commercial trucks and buses—directly behind, along the sides, and sometimes in front—where your vehicle may not be visible to the truck driver. Driving in these areas makes it harder for the truck to see you and to stop or maneuver safely, so you should avoid lingering in them.

question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
options: a:Make you feel better.,b:Help you to be a better driver.,c:Impair your judgment.
note: Drowsiness slows your reaction time, narrows your attention, and impairs your judgment, just like alcohol or drugs. Driving while very tired can cause you to miss hazards, react too slowly, or even fall asleep at the wheel, greatly increasing your crash risk.

question: What do 'No passing zone' signs indicate?
options: a:To maintain a steady speed.,b:That it is not safe and is illegal to pass.,c:To only pass on the left.,d:To speed up slightly.
note: A “No Passing Zone” sign means you must not pass other vehicles in that area. These zones are placed where passing would be especially dangerous, such as on hills, curves, or where you cannot see far enough ahead. When you see this sign, stay in your lane and do not move into the oncoming lane to pass.

question: What is the only medically proven way to remove alcohol or drug combinations from your system?
options: a:Exercise vigorously.,b:Let your body have time.,c:Drink coffee.,d:Take a cold shower.
note: The only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration is to give your body time to process and eliminate the alcohol. Exercise, coffee, cold showers, or other tricks do not speed up this process or make you sober; they may make you feel more awake, but your driving ability is still impaired until enough time has passed.

question: When must vehicles in Arizona be covered by liability insurance?
options: a:Only when driven by a minor.,b:At all times.,c:Only when driven on an interstate.
note: In Arizona, every motor vehicle operated on public roads must be covered by a liability insurance policy at all times. Insurance is not limited to certain drivers or certain types of roads; the vehicle itself must be insured whenever it is being driven.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?
options: a:Turn into the second lane.,b:Turn into the first (closest) lane.,c:Turn into any lane.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn into the first legal lane available, which is the lane closest to you. Starting your turn into the nearest lane helps keep traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles in other lanes.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
options: a:Speed up to get through faster.,b:Use cruise control for stability.,c:Drive at the posted speed.,d:Reduce your speed.
note: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, your tires have less traction and it takes longer to stop. You should slow down below the posted speed limit and drive at a speed that is safe for the conditions, increasing your following distance and making all movements more gradual.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab.,b:Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.,c:Directly behind the body.
note: Large trucks have large blind spots, called "no-zones," where the driver cannot see you. These are directly behind the truck and along both sides, especially the right side, but there is also a blind area immediately to the left of the cab. If you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, the driver probably cannot see you, so avoid lingering in these areas.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, what should you do first?
options: a:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b:Swerve into the lane next to you.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: If another vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, the safest first response is to ease off the accelerator. This immediately begins to increase your following distance without the risk of skidding or losing control that can come from slamming on the brakes or swerving. After easing off the gas, be ready to brake smoothly if needed, but avoid sudden steering movements that could cause a collision in the next lane.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim headlights, you should:
options: a:Look toward the center of the roadway.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look straight ahead.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, the bright light can temporarily blind you. To protect your night vision and still stay safely in your lane, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road, using the white line or road edge as a guide. Do not stare directly into the oncoming headlights, and do not close your eyes or look straight down.

question: Which driving skills can be impaired by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Both alertness and coordination.,b:Alertness.,c:Coordination.
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect multiple driving skills at the same time. They can slow your reaction time, reduce alertness, blur judgment, and interfere with coordination needed for steering, braking, and lane control. Because both alertness and coordination are impaired, any amount of impairment can make driving unsafe, even if you do not feel very affected.

question: When approaching a vehicle from behind at night, when should you switch from high to low beams?
options: a:Within 200 feet.,b:Within 100 feet.,c:Within 50 feet.,d:Within 500 feet.
note: Lower your high beams when you are within 200 feet of another vehicle ahead of you to avoid dazzling the driver.

question: When may you legally drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When you can see clearly in both directions.,b:When the warning lights are not flashing.,c:Never.
note: You must never drive around, under, or through lowered railroad crossing gates. A lowered gate and flashing lights mean a train is approaching, and trains cannot stop quickly. Even if you do not see a train, another train may be coming or may be hidden by curves or obstacles. Always wait until the gates are fully raised and the warning signals have stopped before crossing the tracks.

question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Give the motorcycle a full lane of space when passing.,b:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.,c:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other vehicle. When you pass a motorcycle, you should move fully into the adjacent lane and give the rider the entire lane of space. Never crowd a motorcycle in the same lane or try to force it onto the shoulder.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A U-turn is not permitted:
options: a:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:In a parking lot.
note: A U-turn is generally prohibited on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see oncoming traffic. You must have a clear view and enough distance for other drivers to see you and react safely before you turn.

question: You should not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses because:
options: a:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,b:Large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.,c:Large trucks and buses travel at a higher speeds than small vehicles.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars, so they need a longer distance to stop. If you stop suddenly in front of them, they may not be able to brake in time to avoid a collision. Always leave extra space and avoid cutting closely in front of large vehicles.

question: On slippery surfaces such as snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Avoid using cruise control so you can respond quickly to changes in traction.,b:Increase your following distance to give yourself more time to stop.,c:Shift to a lower gear before descending steep hills.,d:If your vehicle does not have anti-lock brakes, brake gently and avoid locking the wheels.
note: On snow or ice, use a lower gear before going down steep hills to help control your speed without overusing the brakes. Increase your following distance and brake gently. If your vehicle does not have anti-lock brakes, you can use light pumping to avoid locking the wheels; with ABS, apply firm, steady pressure and let the system work.

question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:
options: a:Both be able to safely travel at higher speeds and remain constantly alert.,b:Be constantly alert.,c:Have an HOV pass.,d:Be able to safely travel at higher speeds.
note: Interstate driving involves higher speeds and fast-changing traffic conditions. Safe drivers must be able to handle those higher speeds and stay constantly alert to merging vehicles, lane changes, and sudden slowdowns.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean when the broken line is beside your lane?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line. Drivers next to the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes or passing another vehicle?
options: a:All of the above.,b:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,c:Signal your intention before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you should signal early to communicate your intentions, check your mirrors to see traffic behind and beside you, and check your blind spots by quickly looking over your shoulder. Doing all three helps prevent collisions with vehicles you might not see in your mirrors alone.

question: Consistently looking far ahead while on the highway primarily helps you to:
options: a:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Spot upcoming police officers.,c:Help you keep up with traffic.
note: Looking far ahead on the highway lets you see slowing traffic, lane closures, and other hazards early. This gives you more time to react smoothly, so you brake and steer gradually instead of making sudden, last‑minute moves.

question: After snow or rain, which area is most likely to be slippery?
options: a:A hilly,b:A residential road,c:A road in a shaded area
note: After snow or rain, roads in shaded areas stay wet or icy longer because the sun cannot warm and dry them as quickly. These shaded spots can remain slippery even when the rest of the road looks clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a T intersection from the street that ends, what must a driver do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic.,b:Have the right-of-way.,c:Force their way into traffic.
note: At a T intersection, the driver on the road that ends must yield to vehicles on the through road. You must wait for cross traffic to pass and only enter when it is safe, even if there is no stop sign posted.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, what is the correct action?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid hard braking until the vehicle has slowed.,c:Tap or pump the brakes.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Do not slam on the brakes; hard braking can cause you to lose control, especially at high speeds. Once the vehicle has slowed and you are in control, brake gently as needed and move to a safe place off the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, what should you do to check freeway traffic?
options: a:Using your rearview and side mirrors is sufficient.,b:Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check blind spots.,c:Use your rearview mirror only.
note: When entering a freeway, you must use both your mirrors and a quick glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot before merging. Mirrors alone cannot show vehicles in your blind spots, so a shoulder check helps ensure the lane is clear and that you can merge safely with the flow of traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering freeway traffic from an entrance ramp should:
options: a:Force their way into traffic when necessary.,b:Have the right-of-way.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
note: Drivers entering a freeway must yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge only when there is a safe gap. Do not force your way in or assume other drivers must let you in.

question: When should drivers adjust mirrors, seats, and steering wheel?
options: a:Before starting the vehicle.,b:Before reaching speeds of 55 mph or above.,c:While backing out of a driveway.
note: Before you start driving, adjust your seat so you can reach the pedals and controls comfortably, set your mirrors to minimize blind spots, and position the steering wheel correctly. Doing this before moving ensures good visibility and control, reducing the need for unsafe adjustments while the vehicle is in motion.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if what is true about the other street?
options: a:You increase your speed before the turn.,b:Traffic on that street moves to the left.,c:Traffic on that street moves to the right.
note: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if traffic on the street you are turning onto flows to the left and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Make the turn from the left lane into the left lane of the new street, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic as required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:On the left of the centerline.,b:Near the centerline in the lane closest to the center.,c:In the turn lane two lanes over.,d:Near the right-hand side of the road.
note: For a left turn from a two‑way street, you should be in the lane closest to the centerline, positioned near the centerline so you can turn safely and predictably into the proper lane on the new road. This keeps you out of the path of oncoming traffic and away from the right edge where right‑turning or through traffic may be traveling.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels:
options: a:Toward the edge of the road (right).,b:Straight ahead.,c:Toward the center of the road (left).
note: When parking downhill on a two‑way road with no curb, you turn the front wheels toward the edge of the road so that if the vehicle starts to roll, it will move away from traffic and off the roadway instead of into the travel lane.

question: What can happen if you take prescription drugs while drinking alcohol?
options: a:There will likely be no effect.,b:It may make you more alert.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.,d:It will cancel out alcohol's effects.
note: Alcohol can interact with prescription drugs in ways that greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment. This combination can make you unsafe and legally unfit to drive, even if each substance alone might not have that effect.

question: Fatigue increases the risk of:
options: a:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,b:Being late for an appointment.,c:Missing an exit.
note: Fatigue reduces alertness and slows your reactions. If you become very tired, you can actually fall asleep at the wheel, losing all control of the vehicle and greatly increasing the risk of a serious crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn should you activate your turn signal?
options: a:50 feet.,b:20 feet.,c:100 feet.
note: Signal at least 100 feet before turning to inform other road users of your intentions.

question: If you are already in an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.,b:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,c:Stop.
note: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely. Stopping suddenly in the middle of the intersection can confuse other drivers and increase the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is true about changing lanes safely?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move (right for right lane changes, left for left lane changes).,b:If you have two outside mirrors, you do not need to look over your shoulder.,c:Rely on the turn signal alone.,d:You only need to look over your right shoulder for any lane change.
note: To change lanes safely, you must signal, check your mirrors, and then look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone cannot show everything around your vehicle, so a quick head check helps you see vehicles that may be hidden beside you.

question: It is more dangerous to drive at night because:
options: a:The road is always more slippery at night.,b:Your reaction time is slower at night.,c:You cannot see as far ahead at night.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous mainly because you cannot see as far ahead. Headlights provide limited illumination, which reduces the time you have to see hazards, judge distances, and react safely, especially at higher speeds.

question: If poor weather reduces visibility, what should you do?
options: a:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,b:Increase your following distance.,c:Speed up to get off the road quickly.
