options: a:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,b:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, reduce your speed and be prepared to stop. Pass them cautiously, giving them plenty of space, and never assume they will stay out of the traffic lane.

question: If the broken yellow line is beside your lane when the center is marked with a solid and a broken yellow line, what does it mean?
options: a:You may pass other vehicles to the left when no oncoming traffic is present.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.
note: A centerline with one solid yellow and one broken yellow means passing is allowed only on the side with the broken line. If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may pass when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic; drivers on the solid-line side may not pass.

question: Alcohol at any concentration acts as which of the following?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:An antihistamine.,d:Neither of the above.
note: Alcohol is classified as a depressant. It slows brain and nervous system activity, reducing judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Even small amounts can impair driving ability, which is why you should never drive after drinking.

question: What is the only effective method to remove alcohol from the body?
options: a:Wait.,b:Take a cold shower.,c:Drink strong coffee.,d:Chew gum.
note: Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. Your liver needs time to process alcohol, and nothing else—cold showers, coffee, food, or exercise—can speed up the reduction of your blood alcohol concentration.

question: What should you do about medicine before driving?
options: a:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,b:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about the effects before driving.,c:Have someone follow you home.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can make you drowsy, dizzy, or otherwise impaired. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist how a medicine may affect your driving before you get behind the wheel.

question: At a red traffic light displaying a green arrow for your lane, when may you proceed?
options: a:You wait until the light changes to green.,b:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,c:You first come to a complete stop.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow. If you are in the correct lane and the intersection and crosswalks are clear, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow even though the main red light is on.

question: What is the first ability affected by alcohol?
options: a:Vision.,b:Judgment.,c:Balance.,d:Hearing.
note: Judgment is usually the first ability affected by alcohol. Even small amounts can reduce your ability to make safe decisions, assess risk, and react appropriately, which is why driving after drinking is so dangerous.

question: Which of the following affects how alcohol is absorbed by an individual?
options: a:Intelligence,b:None of the above.,c:Weight,d:Height
note: A person’s weight is one of the main factors that affects how alcohol is absorbed and how high their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) becomes. In general, a smaller person will reach a higher BAC than a larger person after drinking the same amount of alcohol.

question: You should allow an extra cushion of space when following:
options: a:A station wagon.,b:A small passenger car.,c:A driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
note: You should leave extra following distance behind drivers who cannot see the rear of their vehicle, such as large trucks or vehicles towing trailers. The extra space gives you more time to react and helps you stay out of their blind spots.

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, drivers must:
options: a:Pass cautiously at 10 mph.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Stop whenever a school bus is present.,d:Stop only when traveling in the same direction as the bus.
note: You must stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading children, regardless of the direction you are traveling, unless on a divided highway where rules differ.

question: What type of information do blue traffic signs provide?
options: a:Regulatory instructions.,b:Motorist services (rest areas, gas, food, hospitals).,c:Mileage and distance information.,d:Construction and maintenance details.
note: Blue traffic signs provide information about motorist services. They guide drivers to services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals, helping you find essential facilities while traveling.

question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding left, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.,b:Not turn your steering wheel.,c:Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
note: If the rear of your vehicle skids left, you should steer left—toward the direction the rear is sliding. This helps realign the front wheels with the direction of travel and regain control. At the same time, ease off the accelerator and avoid hard braking, which can make the skid worse.

question: When driving at night you should:
options: a:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night, it is harder to see hazards and judge distances, so you should increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights; instead, glance to the right edge of your lane to avoid glare. Use high beams only when appropriate and dim them for oncoming traffic or when following another vehicle.

question: When driving in fog, which lighting choice is recommended?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can actually make it harder to see. Use fog lights if your vehicle has them, and slow down so you can stop within the distance you can see.

question: What should you avoid doing when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Pass the zone carefully and do not slow to 'rubberneck'.,b:Decrease your following distance.,c:Stop to watch the workers.
note: In construction zones, you must keep moving carefully, obey reduced speed limits, and avoid distractions. Never stop just to watch the workers or the work being done. Maintain a safe following distance and avoid slowing down just to look, because sudden slowdowns and distractions increase the risk of rear-end collisions.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction due to water on the road, you should:
options: a:Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.,b:Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.,c:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.
note: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane or lose traction on water, ease off the accelerator and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Do not brake or turn suddenly, because that can cause a skid. Once you feel the tires regain contact with the road, you can gently brake or steer as needed.

question: What do broken yellow lines on the center of the pavement indicate?
options: a:Indicate no passing zones.,b:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and passing is permitted.
note: Broken (dashed) yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line on your side is broken and there are no signs prohibiting it, you may pass another vehicle if it is safe and legal to do so.

question: You can help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away by:
options: a:Maintaining a steady speed.,b:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling early makes your driving more predictable, which helps the driver behind you judge distance and keep a safe following gap. Sudden speed changes or large speed differences increase the risk of rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you enter a left-turn lane with oncoming traffic present, what should you do?
options: a:Stay centered in the left-turn lane.,b:Turn your front wheels to the left while waiting to turn.,c:Signal well in advance of the intersection and keep your wheels straight while waiting.
note: Before turning left, you should signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet before the intersection in city driving (more at higher speeds). As you wait in the left-turn lane, keep your front wheels straight until you actually begin the turn so that if you are hit from behind, your vehicle is less likely to be pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: When is it permissible to pass on the right shoulder of the road?
options: a:Never.,b:When the car ahead is turning left.,c:When the vehicle ahead is driving too slowly.,d:When traffic is stopped in your travel lane.
note: You must not drive off the paved roadway or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle. Passing on the right is only allowed when it can be done on a paved lane or marked roadway, and never by using the shoulder.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,b:Scanning the environment and staying focused on driving.,c:Exceeding the posted speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.
note: Driving faster than the posted speed limit or too fast for weather, traffic, or road conditions greatly increases stopping distance and crash risk. Even if you are under the posted limit, you must slow down when conditions are poor.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal indicates that you should:
options: a:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, watching carefully for other vehicles and pedestrians. You are not required to stop unless it is necessary for safety or to yield to other road users.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are typically what color background?
options: a:Green.,b:White.,c:Yellow.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about traffic laws and regulations, such as speed limits, lane use, and parking rules. In the U.S., these signs are typically white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green letters or symbols on a white background.

question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:
options: a:Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.,b:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,c:Inconvenience drivers.
note: In work zones, barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to guide traffic safely through or around the area and to keep vehicles away from workers and hazards. They help protect both drivers and road workers by clearly marking where you should and should not drive.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
options: a:50 feet,b:75 feet,c:100 feet.
note: You must not park within 50 feet of the nearest rail at a railroad crossing. Parking too close can block visibility or access to the tracks and creates a serious safety hazard if a train approaches.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic.,b:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane and speed up to match traffic.,c:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.
note: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, you must wait for a safe gap in interstate traffic, then accelerate quickly to match the speed of traffic as you merge. Never use the shoulder as a driving lane, and do not force your way into traffic without a safe opening.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should use your horn when:
options: a:Another vehicle is in your way.,b:It may help prevent a collision.,c:Another driver makes a mistake.
note: Use your horn only when it may help prevent a collision or to alert others to a danger. Do not use it just because someone is in your way or made a mistake; unnecessary horn use can startle other drivers and is often illegal.

question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning in wet weather, you should:
options: a:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.,b:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,c:Decrease your speed.
note: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning, slow down and drive smoothly in wet conditions. Lower speeds help your tires push water out of the way and maintain contact with the road. Avoid cruise control and sudden steering or braking on wet roads.

question: At dawn, dusk, and in rain or snow, a good way to let others know you are there is to turn:
options: a:On your parking lights.,b:Up the instrument panel lights.,c:On your headlights.
note: At dawn, dusk, and in rain or snow, turn on your headlights so others can see you more easily. Parking lights or brighter instrument panel lights do not make your vehicle more visible to other road users.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should:
options: a:Allow a larger following distance.,b:Be ready to use your horn.,c:Drive more slowly than posted speeds.
note: Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than cars, and they are harder to see. Leave a larger following distance—at least 3–4 seconds—so you have time to react if the motorcycle slows, swerves, or stops suddenly.

question: If the driver ahead stops at a crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.,b:Change lanes and go around the stopped vehicle.,c:Sound your horn and drive around them.,d:Cautiously pass the vehicle at about 10 mph.
note: If a driver ahead stops at a crosswalk, you must also stop and wait. There may be pedestrians in the crosswalk that you cannot see. Never pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk; remain stopped until you are sure all pedestrians have safely crossed and the crosswalk is clear.

question: If your car begins to skid out of control, you should:
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Stay off the brakes.,c:Apply the brakes lightly.
note: During a skid, braking can make you lose even more control, especially if the wheels lock up. Instead, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go until the tires regain traction.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.
note: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot fully cover. Large trucks have much larger blind spots on all sides, so you should avoid driving alongside them where the truck driver cannot see you.

question: When traveling through a work zone, what should you generally do?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.,b:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop.,c:Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.
note: In work zones, you must slow down, obey posted work zone speed limits, and be ready to stop suddenly for workers, equipment, or lane shifts. Driving more slowly gives you more time to react to unexpected hazards.

question: An orange and red triangular sign on the back of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:Shoulder work ahead.,b:Slow-moving vehicle.,c:The vehicle has the right-of-way.
note: An orange and red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle means it is a slow‑moving vehicle, such as farm equipment or a horse‑drawn wagon. When you see this sign, reduce speed and pass only when it is safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely only on the left side mirror.,d:Signal and immediately change without checking.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone cannot show vehicles in these areas, so a quick head check helps prevent collisions.

question: In a vehicle with airbags, where is it safest for children age 12 and under to ride?
options: a:The back seat.,b:The front seat.,c:The bed of a pick-up truck.
note: Children 12 and under are safest in the back seat, properly restrained in an appropriate child safety seat or seat belt. Airbags in the front seat are designed for adults and can seriously injure small children in a crash, so they should not ride in the front seat when a back seat is available.

question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:You may continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed, if it is clear to do so.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Adjust your mirrors.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn if it is safe and legal, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection. Never assume the way is clear just because the light is green.

question: What can you do to help reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Use your horn frequently.,b:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,c:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.
note: To help prevent road rage, drive predictably and courteously: always signal before changing lanes or turning, avoid cutting other drivers off, obey speed limits, and avoid aggressive gestures or horn use except when needed for safety.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle equipped with ABS, you should:
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: With ABS on snow or ice, press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer where you want to go. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent wheel lockup so you can maintain steering control. Do not pump the brakes yourself.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Must yield to vehicles only on your right.,b:Yield the right-of-way to traffic close enough to cause a conflict.,c:Slow down but never stop.
note: At a yield sign you must slow down and be ready to stop, yielding to any pedestrians and to traffic that is close enough to be a hazard. Enter or proceed only when you can do so without forcing other road users to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: A pedestrian started crossing after the Don't Walk signal began flashing and is in the roadway when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.
note: If a pedestrian is already in the crosswalk when your light turns green, you must wait until they have completely crossed and are safely out of your path. Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are lawfully in the roadway, even if the signal has changed.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, you should:
options: a:Expect the pedestrian to yield to you.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,c:Honk to alert them of your presence.,d:Drive slowly behind them until they move.
note: A person using a guide dog or carrying a white cane is blind or visually impaired and has the absolute right-of-way. You must stop or yield as needed to allow them to cross safely and never honk or pressure them to hurry.

question: What is the primary purpose of rumble strips on the roadway?
options: a:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:Through vibration and sound, they alert drivers that they are leaving their lane or approaching a hazard.,c:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.
note: Rumble strips are raised or grooved patterns on the road that create noise and vibration when you drive over them. This alerts drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, such as a stop sign or work zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels to the right, toward the side of the road.,b:Turn the wheels to the left, toward the center of the road.,c:Point wheels straight ahead.
note: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right, toward the side of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into traffic, reducing the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you arrive at the same time as vehicles on your right and left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,b:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.,c:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Yielding to the vehicle on your right helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals.

question: Why should you use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:To keep your engine warm.,b:So other road users can see your vehicle.,c:To improve fuel efficiency.,d:To warn others of bad weather conditions.
note: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, visibility is reduced, making it harder for others to see your vehicle. Turning on your low‑beam headlights helps other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians see you, which reduces the risk of collisions. Many states also require headlights whenever windshield wipers are in use.

question: If your tires seem to lose contact with the road (hydroplaning), what should you do?
options: a:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,b:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.,c:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and stay off the brakes.
note: When your tires hydroplane, they ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road, so braking or sudden steering can cause a skid. You should gently ease your foot off the accelerator and keep the steering wheel straight until your tires regain traction. Avoid braking or making sudden movements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: It is unlawful to:
options: a:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone or over a railroad crossing.,b:Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing only.,c:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone only.
note: Passing is prohibited in marked no‑passing zones and at railroad crossings because sight distance and stopping distance may be limited, and unexpected hazards can appear. You must obey no‑passing markings and signs and never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing.

question: If you are crossing an intersection when an emergency vehicle with siren and lights approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.,c:Continue through the intersection
note: If an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches and you are already in an intersection, you should continue through the intersection to clear it safely. Once you are out of the intersection, pull to the right side of the road and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

question: If you approach an intersection showing a steady yellow light and have not entered it, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Come to a safe stop.,c:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection and can stop safely, you must slow down and come to a safe stop before the intersection. Do not speed up to beat the red light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.
note: When waiting to turn left, you should keep your wheels pointed straight ahead until you actually start turning. If your wheels are turned and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. When parked on a hill or sloping driveway, you should turn your wheels so that if the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic, not straight ahead.

question: Which statement about bicyclists is correct?
options: a:Should ride facing traffic.,b:Must follow the same laws as motorists.,c:Must stay in the right lane.
note: Bicyclists generally must obey the same traffic laws as drivers of motor vehicles: they ride in the same direction as traffic, stop at signals and signs, and yield when required. They also have the same rights to use the roadway, except where specifically prohibited.

question: When merging onto an interstate, you should:
options: a:Merge across two lanes at once.,b:Select a safe gap and merge into traffic.,c:Always stop at the end of the ramp.,d:Enter at any speed and slow down once merged.
note: When merging onto an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and then merge into a safe gap. Do not stop on the ramp unless absolutely necessary, and never merge across multiple lanes at once.

question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed when:
options: a:Driving on level roads.,b:Driving up long or steep hills.,c:Driving down long or steep hills.
note: Large trucks are heavy and require more power to climb. They typically lose speed when driving up long or steep hills because it is harder for them to maintain momentum. When following a truck uphill, be prepared for it to slow down and adjust your following distance accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:
options: a:Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.,b:Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.,c:Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
note: When passing, you must not assume other drivers will slow down or leave space for you. Instead, only begin passing when you are sure you have enough clear distance to pass safely and return to your lane without relying on the other driver to help you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,b:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.,c:Turn left and find another route.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it, even if the light is green. Entering when traffic is stopped ahead can leave you blocking the intersection, which is unsafe and often illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The posted maximum speed limit should be driven only under what conditions?
options: a:During the day.,b:During the night.,c:Under ideal conditions.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed in ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions are less than ideal, such as in heavy traffic, bad weather, poor visibility, or on rough or winding roads.

question: Which statement best describes how a defensive driver thinks?
options: a:They expect no breaks and give none.,b:They anticipate other drivers' possible actions and prepare to react.,c:They assume other drivers will always do the right thing.,d:They rely only on traffic signals.
note: A defensive driver constantly scans the road, expects that other drivers may make mistakes, and is ready to react safely. They do not assume others will always follow the rules; instead, they anticipate possible actions and leave space and time to respond.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the bloodstream may affect a driver's:
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge of traffic laws.,d:License class.
note: Even a small amount of alcohol can slow your reactions and affect your judgment, coordination, and ability to make safe driving decisions. You do not need to feel drunk for your driving to be impaired.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:
options: a:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.,b:Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.,c:Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.
note: At night you must drive slowly enough that you can stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. Overdriving your headlights is dangerous because hazards may appear beyond your stopping distance.

question: Traffic control devices in construction and maintenance work areas are what color?
options: a:Red.,b:Orange.,c:Yellow.
note: Orange is the standard color for construction and maintenance work zone signs, cones, and barriers. When you see orange traffic control devices, expect workers, lane shifts, and reduced speeds, and be prepared to slow down and drive with extra caution.

question: How can you best know where traffic is behind you?
options: a:Keep vehicles out of your blind spots only.,b:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,c:Turn and look out your back window constantly.,d:Use only side mirrors.
note: You best know where traffic is behind you by frequently checking your rearview mirror. Regular mirror checks help you track vehicles approaching from the rear, notice fast‑closing traffic, and prepare for lane changes or stops. You still need to check side mirrors and blind spots, but the rearview mirror is your primary tool for monitoring traffic directly behind you.

question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:
options: a:Other drivers when they want to slow down.,b:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,c:The truck driver to stop the vehicle.
note: Large trucks are heavy and need much more distance to stop than passenger cars. Extra space in front of a truck gives the truck driver room to slow or stop safely if traffic changes. Cutting in front of a truck or following too closely in front of it reduces this stopping space and greatly increases the risk of a rear‑end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should never:
options: a:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.,b:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.
note: When changing lanes, you should never change lanes abruptly or without planning. Safe lane changes require signaling in advance, checking mirrors, and looking over your shoulder to clear your blind spot. Sudden, un-signaled lane changes surprise other drivers and can easily cause sideswipe or rear‑end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly turn before the truck or bus can.,b:Wait until the truck or bus completes the turn before you turn.,c:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.
note: When a truck or bus is making a right turn, you should wait until it completes the turn before you turn. Large vehicles often swing wide or start from a left position to make a right turn, and they may need extra space between their right side and the curb. Never try to squeeze between the vehicle and the curb or cut in front of it, as you can easily end up in the driver’s blind spot and be hit or pinned.

question: When is pavement most slippery during rainy conditions?
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:If it has been raining all day.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: Pavement is most slippery during the first part of a rainstorm. Oil, grease, and dust that have built up on the road mix with the fresh rainwater and create a slick film. After it has rained for a while, much of this residue is washed away and the road surface generally becomes less slippery, though drivers should still use caution.

question: If your car becomes disabled on the highway, you should:
options: a:Stop in the right travel lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled portion of the highway if possible.,c:Stop where you are and leave the vehicle.,d:Turn on high beams to signal for help.
note: If your vehicle becomes disabled, you should move it as far off the traveled portion of the roadway as possible, ideally with all four wheels off the road. This reduces the chance of being struck by passing traffic. Once safely off the road, turn on your hazard lights and stay clear of moving traffic while you arrange for help.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Keep driving at a steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop.,c:Honk to get the pedestrian to move over.
note: When you face both an oncoming vehicle and a pedestrian ahead, you should deal with one hazard at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first so you have more space and time. Then, when it is safe, move around the pedestrian while giving them plenty of room. Never force a pedestrian to move or assume others will stop for you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach the top of a hill, how should you prepare?
options: a:Speed up slightly.,b:Reduce speed and be prepared to stop.,c:Maintain a steady speed.
note: As you approach the top of a hill, you cannot see what is ahead, such as stopped traffic, a slow vehicle, or an obstacle. You should reduce your speed and be prepared to stop if needed. Simply maintaining speed or speeding up is unsafe when your view is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you continually pass other vehicles on a two-lane road by driving faster than others, you will:
options: a:Help prevent traffic congestion.,b:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.,c:Increase your chances of a collision.
note: Frequently passing other vehicles on a two-lane road usually means you are driving faster than the flow of traffic and repeatedly entering the oncoming lane. This increases your risk of head-on collisions and other crashes, especially where sight distance is limited. Staying with the flow of traffic and passing only when necessary and clearly safe is much safer.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on a red light after stopping?
options: a:Whenever you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.,b:When you are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,c:When you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.
note: In most U.S. states, you may turn left on red only when you are turning from a one‑way street onto another one‑way street, after coming to a complete stop and yielding to all traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign specifically prohibits the turn.

question: Within how many days must you notify the MVD of an address change?
options: a:10 days.,b:30 days.,c:45 days.,d:60 days.
note: Arizona law requires you to notify the MVD within 10 days when your name or address changes so that your driving record and license information stay current and official notices can reach you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass on a two-lane road you should:
options: a:Flash your headlights as you pass.,b:Sound your horn as you pass.,c:Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
note: Before passing on a two‑lane road, you must be sure there is enough clear distance ahead to complete the pass safely, including time to move into the oncoming lane, pass the vehicle, and return to your lane without interfering with oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic after parking at a curb, you should:
options: a:Enter after the first two vehicles pass.,b:Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Wait for a large enough gap to get up to the speed of traffic.
note: When pulling out from a curb, wait for a gap that lets you accelerate smoothly up to the speed of traffic without forcing other drivers to brake or swerve; always signal and check mirrors and blind spots before moving.

question: How far ahead should a driver typically look in city driving to avoid sudden stops or turns?
options: a:Three city blocks.,b:Five feet.,c:One city block.
note: In city driving, you should scan the road at least one city block ahead so you can see traffic lights, pedestrians, and potential hazards early and adjust your speed or lane position smoothly instead of making sudden stops or turns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to drive on the shoulder to pass a car?
options: a:If the shoulder is wide enough.,b:If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You must not drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle. The shoulder is for emergencies and stopped vehicles, not for travel or passing. Passing on the shoulder is unsafe because other drivers do not expect moving traffic there and it is generally illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is passing you in a no passing zone, how should you respond?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: If another driver is passing you illegally, your goal is to reduce the risk of a crash, not to enforce the law. Gently slowing down gives the passing driver more space and time to return to the lane safely. Do not speed up or block them; cooperate so everyone stays safe.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, how should you proceed?
options: a:Quickly swerve into the next lane.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: Animals near the road can suddenly run into your path. Slow down, cover the brake, and pass with plenty of space so you can stop or steer smoothly if they move. Do not swerve suddenly or speed up, as that can cause you to lose control or hit another vehicle.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road indicates:
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from either direction.,c:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,d:A construction zone is ahead.
note: A broken yellow center line separates traffic moving in opposite directions and allows passing from either direction when it is safe. You may cross the line to pass only if you have enough clear distance ahead and no oncoming traffic or other hazards.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags, what should you still do?
options: a:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.,b:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,c:Seat belts should still be worn.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. Always wear your lap and shoulder belt properly, even in a vehicle with airbags, to keep you in position and reduce the risk of serious injury in a crash.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what should you expect?
options: a:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.,b:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,c:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
note: Orange construction signs and cones indicate a work zone. You should expect workers, equipment, lane shifts, and reduced speeds ahead, and be prepared to slow down or stop as needed.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Reaction time and coordination.,b:Alertness and concentration.,c:All of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect the brain and nervous system, which slows reaction time, reduces coordination, and harms alertness and concentration. Because all of these skills are affected, all of the listed choices are impaired.

question: Which practice blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,b:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.
note: Slowing down just to look at a collision or anything unusual on the road—called rubbernecking—disrupts the smooth flow of traffic, causes sudden slowdowns, and can lead to more crashes.

question: [Removed - image-based question]
options: a:Right turns only.,b:Right turns permitted.,c:No passing zone.
note: A yellow pennant-shaped sign placed on the left side of the road marks the beginning of a no passing zone, warning you not to pass other vehicles in that area.

question: If involved in a minor intersection collision with no injuries and little damage, you should:
options: a:Drive away if damage is minor.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.,c:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.,d:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
note: If you are in a minor crash with no injuries and the vehicles can be moved, you should safely move them out of the traffic lane. This helps prevent additional collisions and keeps traffic flowing while you exchange information and, if needed, wait for law enforcement.

question: Which lights should you use in fog, rain, or snow to avoid reducing visibility?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.
note: Low beam headlights are correct in fog, rain, or snow because their light pattern aims down toward the road and is less likely to reflect off moisture in the air. High beams can bounce back from fog, rain, or snow and create glare, making it harder to see. Four‑way flashers are for emergencies or stopped vehicles, not for normal driving in bad weather.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, it is safe to move back into the right lane when:
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:You can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: When you pass another vehicle, you should not move back into the right lane until you can clearly see the front of the vehicle you passed in your interior rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead of that vehicle and reduces the risk of cutting them off or forcing them to brake suddenly.

question: How much space should you normally leave between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:One second,b:10 seconds,c:Three to six seconds
note: A three‑ to six‑second following distance under normal conditions gives you time to see and react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. You pick a fixed object, note when the vehicle ahead passes it, and count seconds until you pass the same object. In bad weather, at higher speeds, or in heavy traffic, you should increase this following distance.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair driving.,b:Drugs have no effect when combined with alcohol.,c:Only illegal drugs can impair driving.,d:Prescriptions are always safe if you feel fine.
note: Even over‑the‑counter and prescription medications can slow your reactions, make you drowsy, or affect judgment, and it is illegal to drive if any drug impairs your ability to operate a vehicle safely. Illegal drugs, prescription drugs, and common cold or allergy medicines can all impair driving, especially when combined with alcohol.

question: Which lights improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Low beam headlights are the best choice in rain or fog because they light the road ahead without causing as much glare. High beams can reflect off water droplets or fog and shine back into your eyes, reducing how far you can see. Parking lights alone do not provide enough light to see or be seen safely while moving.

question: How are bicycles treated on roadways?
options: a:As toys.,b:As vehicles.,c:As hazards.,d:As pedestrians.
note: On public roads, bicycles are treated as vehicles. Bicyclists generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles, including obeying traffic signals, signs, and lane rules. Drivers must share the road and yield to bicycles as they would to other vehicles when required by law.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what must you do?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,b:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk.

question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Fog lights only.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams help you see the road and help others see you without excessive glare.

question: Must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,b:At all times.,c:Only if a crossing guard is present.
note: You must always yield the right-of-way to a blind pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog. Stop well before the crosswalk or where they are crossing, and do not honk or try to direct them; allow them to cross safely at their own pace.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit when approaching a school crossing if no other limit is posted?
options: a:25 mph.,b:15 mph.,c:10 mph.
note: School-zone speed limits are set by each state and can vary; common limits include 15, 20, or 25 mph when children are present or during posted times. Because there is no single standard unposted school-crossing speed limit across the U.S., you must follow the specific speed limit signs and your state’s driver handbook for the correct value in your area.

question: When exiting the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill, you should:
options: a:Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.,b:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.,c:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
note: When exiting a freeway on a downhill curve, you should slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve. Braking hard while already in the curve, especially on a downhill, can cause your vehicle to skid or lose traction. By reducing speed in advance, you maintain better control and can safely follow the curve of the ramp.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arizona's GDL program, what passenger restrictions apply during the first six months of holding a Class G graduated driver license?
options: a:No passengers under age 18 are permitted,b:No more than one passenger under age 18 is permitted (unless they are siblings or accompanied by a parent/guardian),c:Only family members are permitted as passengers,d:No passenger restrictions apply
note: In Arizona, Class G license holders under age 18 are restricted from carrying more than one passenger under age 18 during the first six months, except for immediate siblings or when accompanied by a parent/guardian.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the nighttime driving curfew for a minor holding a Class G Graduated Driver License in Arizona?
options: a:10:00 PM to 5:00 AM,b:11:00 PM to 5:00 AM,c:Midnight to 5:00 AM,d:1:00 AM to 5:00 AM
note: Graduated Class G license holders under 18 in Arizona may not drive between midnight and 5:00 AM unless driving to/from school, work, church, or in an emergency, or accompanied by a licensed parent/guardian.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum auto liability insurance coverage required for all motor vehicles registered in Arizona?
note: Arizona requires motor vehicle liability insurance coverage of 25/50/15: $25,000 for bodily injury per person, $50,000 for bodily injury per accident, and $15,000 for property damage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arizona law, what is the default speed limit in any business or residential district unless otherwise posted?
options: a:15 mph,b:20 mph,c:25 mph,d:30 mph
note: The statutory speed limit in any business or residential district in Arizona is 25 mph unless a different speed limit is posted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit when approaching a school crossing in Arizona?
options: a:10 mph,b:15 mph,c:20 mph,d:25 mph
note: In Arizona, the speed limit when approaching a school crossing is 15 mph. Fines for speeding in school zones are doubled.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Arizona Revised Statutes, what is the minimum property damage threshold that requires a law enforcement officer to complete a written accident report?
note: Arizona law (A.R.S. § 28-667) requires investigating officers to complete a written accident report for any crash that results in injury, death, or total property damage exceeding $2,000.
